title: Possible precision loss in write_toml() for higher-precision numeric values
description:
Thank you for maintaining `{toml}`!

I came across what may be unintended behavior in `write_toml()` when serializing higher-precision numeric values from R. In my local testing, the written TOML appears to reduce numeric precision to roughly 4 decimal places, and that reduced precision then persists after round-tripping with `parse_toml()`.

I wanted to check whether this is expected behavior, a known limitation of the current serializer, or something that might be worth documenting or revisiting.

### Reprex

```r
library(toml)

original <- list(
  value1 = 73.4169120128073,
  value2 = 0.223545331529093
)

written <- write_toml(original)
parsed <- parse_toml(written)

written
parsed
parsed$value1 - original$value1
parsed$value2 - original$value2
```

### What I observed

`write_toml()` produced:

```r
value1 = 73.4169
value2 = 0.2235
```

and parsing that result gave back the truncated values rather than the original double values.

### What I expected

I had expected either:

1. the full numeric precision of the input doubles to be preserved in the serialized TOML, or
2. a user-facing option to control numeric formatting or precision during serialization.

### Why this matters

This came up in a configuration-generation workflow where numeric values are read from source data at higher precision and then written to TOML. In that kind of workflow, small changes introduced during serialization can persist on round-trip and may be difficult to spot.

### Documentation note

I may have missed it, but I did not see an argument in `?write_toml` for controlling numeric precision.

### Session info

- `toml` version: `1.1.0`
- R version: `4.6.0`

If this behavior is expected, a brief note in the documentation would already be helpful. If not, I would be happy to provide any additional details or test cases. Thank you!
